title: Impact of Upcoming Fairer Workplace Legislation on Workplace Culture And Current Approaches to Deal With Workplace Discrimination
what_it_is: Impact of Upcoming Fairer Workplace Legislation on Workplace Culture And Current Approaches to Deal With Workplace Discrimination

sections.label: Workplace discrimination legislation questions
sections.summary: Questions ask the Minister for Manpower about the scope, progress, rollout date, union roles, and consultations for proposed workplace discrimination legislation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower with regard to the proposed legislation on workplace discrimination (a) what are the scope, progress and expected rollout date; (b) what will be the role of unions, union leaders and tripartite partners in the implementation and execution of this law; and (c) whether there will be ground and stakeholder consultations in the promulgation process.

sections.label: TAFEP guidelines and discrimination cases
sections.summary: Questions ask about timelines for legislating TAFEP guidelines, resolving disputes, costs at the Employment Claims Tribunal, and gender discrimination case numbers.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) whether the Ministry can provide a timeline on how long it will take for the TAFEP guidelines to be enshrined into our laws; (b) what is the projected timeline to resolve employment disputes, from conciliation and mediation to the Employment Claims Tribunal; (c) whether any party is expected to shoulder any costs if the matter is taken to the Employment Claims Tribunal; and (d) whether the anti-discrimination laws will apply during the interview and recruitment stage.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) in the past three years, how many workplace discrimination cases filed with the Ministry are gender discrimination in nature; (b) what are the top three types of gender-related discrimination filed; (c) how many are resolved via current platforms like the Tripartite Alliance for Dispute Management and Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices; and (d) with the proposed tribunal system, how will the Ministry enhance the recourse and remedial actions, especially for gender-related workplace discrimination.

sections.label: Legislating Tripartite Guidelines decision
sections.summary: The Government recognised calls by Members to legislate the Tripartite Guidelines and concluded legislation could be a helpful next step.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: We recognised the calls made by Members in this House previously, including Mr Patrick Tay, Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Mr Louis Ng, for the Tripartite Guidelines to be legislated.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: We concluded that legislation could be a helpful next step to take and updated the Prime Minister on our assessment.

sections.label: Broadening remedies through legislation
sections.summary: With legislation, the range of remedies available can be broadened.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: With legislation, we can broaden the range of remedies available.

sections.label: Tripartite Committee work timeline
sections.summary: The Tripartite Committee aims to complete its work in the first half of 2022, after which the Government will consider its recommendations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The Tripartite Committee aims to complete its work in the first half of 2022.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The Government will then consider its recommendations and, if accepted, start work to prepare legislation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: In the meantime, I would like to reiterate that TAFEP and MOM will ensure the Tripartite Guidelines continue to be practised and upheld.
